title: Nadella: Here's why Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees
html:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella commented at the New York Times Dealbook Summit on why the company offered severance packages to approximately 60,000 employees in October to encourage them to voluntarily leave their jobs.

According to Nadella, it’s not that AI will replace programmers, for example, but rather that their roles are fundamentally changing. As an example, he cited a development team working on Cowork in Microsoft 365 that consists of only 11 people.

“They’re building a software factory that builds the product. They’re not building the product themselves,” said Nadella, as reported by TechCrunch.

He believes that the same trend could affect virtually every profession. But the transition will be particularly challenging for an established company like Microsoft, which wasn’t built from the ground up around AI.

According to Nadella, the changes may be difficult for some employees, and the voluntary separation offer was intended to give employees the opportunity to choose whether they want to be part of the transition or leave the company.

This article originally appeared on Computer Sweden.
summary: The choice: Prepare for AI to radically change your job or take the money and run.
